examples.ko: 벽에 나사못을 네 개 박아서 선반을 달았어요.
examples.en: I put four screws into the wall and hung a shelf.
The screws are loose, so the chair keeps wobbling.

examples.ko: 나사못 길이가 너무 짧아서 다시 사러 가야 해요.
examples.en: The screws are too short, so I have to go buy them again.
Turn the screw with a screwdriver and tighten it firmly.
There is a screw on the floor, so be careful.

examples.ko: 이 책상은 나사못 없이도 조립할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can assemble this desk even without screws.

explain: '못'은 망치로 박고 나사못은 드라이버로 돌려서 박아요. 일상에서는 줄여서 '나사'라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: A '못' (nail) is hammered in, while a 나사못 is turned in with a screwdriver. In daily talk people often shorten it to just '나사'.

examples.en: When I cut the tree, the annual rings were clearly visible.

examples.ko: 나이테를 세어 보면 나무가 몇 살인지 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you count the rings, you can tell how old the tree is.

examples.ko: 이 나무는 나이테 간격이 아주 촘촘해요.
examples.en: This tree's rings are very close together.
The rings remain as circles on the stump.
The teacher showed us a photo of tree rings.
One more ring is added every year.

explain: 나무 이야기에만 쓰고 사람 나이에는 쓰지 않아요. 한자어로 '연륜'이라고도 하지만 일상에서는 '나이테'를 더 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is used only for trees, never for a person's age. The Sino-Korean word '연륜' also exists, but in daily life 나이테 is more common.

examples.en: You're old enough, so please act your age.

examples.ko: 나잇값을 못 하는 어른을 보면 실망해요.
examples.en: I'm disappointed when I see adults who don't act their age.

examples.ko: 형은 어릴 때부터 나잇값을 톡톡히 했어요.
examples.en: My older brother has acted maturely for his age since he was little.
I'm over thirty, so I should live up to my age.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 나잇값도 못 하고 매번 화만 내요.
examples.en: He doesn't act his age and just gets angry every time.
I want to be an adult who acts his age.

explain: 거의 '나잇값을 하다/못 하다' 모양으로만 써요. 못 할 때 나무라는 말투로 많이 나와서 윗사람에게 직접 하면 무례해요.
explain_en: It is almost always used as '나잇값을 하다/못 하다'. It often carries a scolding tone when someone fails to do so, so saying it directly to an elder is rude.

examples.ko: 요즘 나잇살 때문에 바지가 안 맞아요.
examples.en: These days my pants don't fit because of age-related weight gain.
I haven't exercised, so I've put on weight with age.
They say age-related fat isn't easy to lose.

examples.ko: 마흔이 넘으니 나잇살이 배에 붙기 시작했어요.
examples.en: After forty, fat started to build up on my belly.
Worried about gaining weight with age, I walk every evening.
My friend sighed that he had gained weight with age.

explain: '나잇살이 붙다/찌다'로 자주 쓰고, 나이 들어 느는 살을 농담처럼 가볍게 말할 때 어울려요. 진지한 건강 이야기에서는 그냥 '체중이 늘다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is often used as '나잇살이 붙다/찌다' and suits a light, joking tone about weight gained with age. In a serious health talk people just say '체중이 늘다'.

en: fall down; tumble down; be thrown down

examples.en: I slipped on the ice and fell flat on my back.
The child was startled and just fell over.
The chair broke and I tumbled over backward.
It's really embarrassing to fall flat on the street.
Be careful not to fall on the snowy road.

examples.ko: 동생은 공을 차다가 나자빠져서 웃음거리가 됐어요.
examples.en: My younger brother fell over while kicking the ball and became a laughingstock.

explain: '넘어지다'보다 벌렁 뒤로 쓰러지는 느낌이 강한 입말이에요. '일은 안 하고 나자빠져 있다'처럼 빈둥거리며 누워 있다는 뜻으로도 써요.
explain_en: Compared with '넘어지다', it suggests flopping over backward and is a spoken word. It can also mean lying around idly, as in '일은 안 하고 나자빠져 있다'.

examples.en: I sang a lullaby softly to the child.

examples.ko: 그는 창가에서 나지막이 내 이름을 불렀어요.
examples.en: He called my name softly by the window.
Please speak in a low voice in the library.

examples.ko: 영숙은 친구 귀에 대고 나지막이 말했어요.
examples.en: Yeongsuk put her mouth to her friend's ear and said in a low voice.
Low houses are clustered at the foot of the mountain.
The teacher spoke in a low, whispering voice.

explain: 소리가 낮을 때도, 건물이나 언덕의 높이가 낮을 때도 써요. '낮게'보다 조용하고 부드러운 느낌이고, '나직이'도 비슷하게 써요.
explain_en: It describes a low voice and also low-lying buildings or hills. It feels quieter and softer than '낮게', and '나직이' is used in a similar way.

examples.ko: 아침에 일어나 보니 나팔꽃이 활짝 피었어요.
examples.en: When I woke up in the morning, the morning glories were in full bloom.
The child planted morning glory seeds in a pot.

examples.ko: 나팔꽃은 해가 뜨면 피고 오후에는 시들어요.
examples.en: Morning glories open when the sun rises and wilt in the afternoon.
Morning glory vines climb along the fence.
The morning glory is purple and so pretty.
I observed morning glories for my summer vacation homework.

explain: 꽃 모양이 나팔 같아서 붙은 이름이에요. 초등학교 여름방학 관찰 숙제에 자주 나오는 꽃이에요.
explain_en: The name comes from the flower's trumpet-like shape. It is a flower that often appears in elementary school summer observation homework.

examples.en: My math test score this time was a failing grade.

examples.ko: 낙제점을 받아서 방학에 보충 수업을 들어요.
examples.en: I got a failing grade, so I take a makeup class during vacation.
This restaurant's hygiene deserves a failing grade.
I studied all night to avoid a failing grade.
The evaluation said customer satisfaction was at a failing level.
My younger brother hid his report card with a failing grade.

explain: 학교 성적뿐 아니라 서비스, 정책, 사람의 태도를 평가할 때도 비유로 많이 써요. '낙제점을 받다'로 자주 말하고, 반대로는 '합격점'을 써요.
explain_en: Besides school grades, it is often used figuratively to judge services, policies or someone's attitude. It commonly appears as '낙제점을 받다', and the opposite is '합격점'.

examples.ko: 다행히 낙제를 면해서 다음 학기에 올라갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: Luckily I avoided failing, so I can move up next semester.
If I fail this time, I have to repeat the first year.

examples.ko: 그 식당의 심사 결과는 맛은 합격이고 위생은 낙제였어요.
examples.en: In that restaurant's review, taste passed but hygiene failed.
To avoid failing, you need at least 60 points.
I'm worried I might fail math.
My friend is upset because he failed his English class.

explain: 시험에 '떨어지다'와 달리 과목이나 학년의 기준에 못 미쳐서 통과하지 못할 때 써요. 반대말은 '합격하다'나 '통과하다'이고, '낙제를 면하다'로 자주 말해요.
explain_en: Unlike '떨어지다' for failing an exam, it is used when you miss the standard for a subject or school year. The opposites are '합격하다' or '통과하다', and '낙제를 면하다' is a common phrase.

examples.ko: 낚싯줄이 여러 가닥으로 꼬여서 풀기가 힘들어요.
examples.en: The fishing line is tangled in many strands and hard to untie.
A big fish bit, and the fishing line became taut.
I replaced the fishing line with a new one.
You attach a hook and bait to the end of the fishing line.
The fishing line got caught on a branch and snapped.
My father slowly reeled in the fishing line.

explain: 맞춤법에서 '낚시줄'이 아니라 사이시옷을 넣은 '낚싯줄'이 표준 표기예요. 낚싯대, 낚싯바늘처럼 낚시 도구 이름이 이렇게 이어져요.
explain_en: The standard spelling includes the 사이시옷, so it is '낚싯줄', not '낚시줄'. Other fishing gear names such as 낚싯대 and 낚싯바늘 follow the same pattern.

examples.en: A pickpocket snatched my bag.
The eagle snatched the fish in an instant.
The child snatched the phone out of my hand.
He snatched the ball and ran straight toward the goal.
Someone snatched my umbrella and ran off.

examples.ko: 그 팀이 경기 막판에 역전 기회를 낚아챘어요.
examples.en: That team seized the chance for a comeback late in the game.

explain: 갑자기 힘 있게 잡아서 가져가는 순간적인 동작이에요. '빼앗다'는 억지로 가져가는 뜻이 강하고, 낚아채다는 재빠른 손동작이 눈에 보이는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is a sudden, forceful grab that takes something away in a moment. '빼앗다' stresses taking by force, while 낚아채다 gives a vivid picture of a quick hand movement.

examples.en: Three crucian carp were caught today.

examples.ko: 광고 제목에 낚여서 영상을 끝까지 봤어요.
examples.en: I got hooked by the ad title and watched the video to the end.

examples.ko: 자극적인 기사 제목에 낚이지 않게 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful not to be lured by sensational headlines.
Before I knew it, I fell for my friend's prank.

examples.ko: 낚였다는 걸 알고 나서 웃음이 나왔어요.
examples.en: After realizing I'd been tricked, I laughed.
Fish are easily caught with this bait.

explain: 물고기가 잡힌다는 뜻 외에, 요즘은 자극적인 제목에 속아서 클릭했을 때 '낚였다'고 말해요. 가볍고 장난스러운 입말이라 공식적인 글에는 잘 안 써요.
explain_en: Besides a fish being caught, people nowadays say '낚였다' when they were fooled into clicking on a sensational title. It is light, playful spoken language and is not used much in formal writing.

examples.en: The plane hit turbulence and shook a lot.

examples.ko: 난기류 때문에 기내 서비스가 잠시 중단됐어요.
examples.en: In-flight service was paused for a while because of turbulence.

examples.ko: 난기류 구간에서는 안전벨트를 꼭 매야 해요.
examples.en: You must fasten your seat belt in turbulent areas.
The flight attendant announced that turbulence was expected.
I was startled by the turbulence and spilled my coffee.
This flight had severe turbulence and it was scary.

explain: 비행기를 탈 때 방송이나 뉴스에서 자주 들어요. 일상 대화에서는 '비행기가 많이 흔들렸어요'처럼 풀어서 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: The negotiations between the two countries ran into turbulence.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 순조롭지 않고 불안정해졌다는 비유로 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative use common in the news meaning things became rocky and unstable.

explain_en: You often hear it in flight announcements and the news. In daily talk people also describe it in plain words like '비행기가 많이 흔들렸어요'.

examples.en: We sat around the stove and ate sweet potatoes.
The cat is dozing by the heater.
On cold days I want to sit by the heater.
I hung the wet gloves near the heater.
Grandmother told us old stories by the stove.
Don't get too close to the heater.

explain: 바닷가, 길가, 강가처럼 '-가'가 붙어 '곁'을 나타내요. 소리 때문에 사이시옷이 들어가서 '난로가'가 아니라 '난롯가'라고 써요.
explain_en: Like 바닷가, 길가 and 강가, the '-가' ending means the area beside something. A 사이시옷 is added, so it is written '난롯가', not '난로가'.

examples.ko: 전쟁을 피해 온 사람들이 난민촌에서 지내요.
examples.en: People who fled the war are staying in a refugee camp.
The news reported on winter life in the refugee camp.
They say water and medicine are lacking in the refugee camp.
A volunteer group sent blankets to the refugee camp.

examples.ko: 난민촌 아이들을 위한 학교가 문을 열었어요.
examples.en: A school for children in the refugee camp has opened.

examples.ko: 난민촌의 모습을 사진으로 본 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I have seen the refugee camp in photos.

explain: 뉴스나 기부 광고에서 주로 나오는 말이에요. 같은 뜻으로 '난민 캠프'라고도 하지만 기사에서는 '난민촌'이 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: This word mostly appears in the news and donation ads. People also say '난민 캠프', but articles tend to use 난민촌.

en: very first time; first time in one's life

examples.en: I rode an airplane for the first time in my life.
I went on a trip alone for the first time in my life.
It was food I had never seen before, so I was a bit scared.
I came first for the very first time and was really happy.

examples.ko: 저는 난생처음 김치를 직접 담가 봤어요.
examples.en: I made kimchi by myself for the first time in my life.

examples.ko: 난생처음 겪는 일이라 어떻게 해야 할지 몰랐어요.
examples.en: It was my first experience ever, so I didn't know what to do.

explain: 그냥 '처음'이 아니라 태어나서 지금까지 한 번도 없었다는 놀라움을 강조해요. 보통 '난생처음 + 동사'처럼 부사처럼 바로 동사 앞에 쓰고, '생전 처음'도 비슷하게 말해요.
explain_en: Rather than a plain 'first', it stresses surprise that this has never happened since you were born. It usually sits right before a verb like an adverb, and '생전 처음' is used in a similar way.

examples.en: The bird flapped its wings strongly and took off.
The butterfly's wing flapping looks very light.
The baby bird started clumsy flapping of its wings.
I can hear the buzzing of the bee's wings.
A hummingbird flaps its wings dozens of times a second.

examples.ko: 날갯짓 몇 번에 새는 하늘 높이 올랐어요.
examples.en: With a few flaps of its wings, the bird rose high into the sky.

explain: '날갯짓하다'처럼 동사로도 쓰고, '날개를 퍼덕이다'보다 움직임을 짧게 말하는 느낌이에요. '새로운 날갯짓을 시작하다'처럼 도전의 시작을 비유할 때도 있어요.
explain_en: It can also be used as the verb '날갯짓하다', and it sounds more compact than '날개를 퍼덕이다'. It is sometimes used figuratively, as in '새로운 날갯짓을 시작하다', for starting a new challenge.

examples.ko: 탈이 날까 봐 날것은 먹지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't eat raw food in case I get sick.
This shop also sells chicken raw.

examples.ko: 날것과 익힌 음식은 도마를 따로 쓰세요.
examples.en: Use separate cutting boards for raw and cooked food.
I dislike the unique smell of raw food.
If you eat vegetables raw, they are crunchy.
You shouldn't feed raw food to a child.

explain: 익히지 않은 음식을 말하고 반대는 '익힌 것'이에요. '생것'이라고도 하고, '날것 그대로의 감정'처럼 꾸미지 않은 모습을 비유할 때도 있어요.
explain_en: It refers to uncooked food, and the opposite is '익힌 것'. People also say '생것', and it can be used figuratively for unpolished things, as in '날것 그대로의 감정'.

examples.en: Small flies keep swarming in the kitchen.
I left fruit out and fruit flies appeared.

examples.ko: 날파리 때문에 음식물 쓰레기를 바로 버렸어요.
examples.en: Because of the flies, I threw out the food waste right away.
It looks like little flies are floating in front of my eyes.
I made a vinegar trap to catch the fruit flies.
In summer there are more small flies and it's tough.

explain: 과일 주변의 초파리뿐 아니라 집 안에 꼬이는 작은 날벌레를 넓게 가리키는 입말이에요. 정확히 말할 때는 '초파리'라고 해요.
explain_en: In speech it covers not only fruit flies but small flying insects around the house in general. When you want to be exact, you say '초파리'.

examples.en: Since the fight, we act like strangers.
He was a stranger I met on the street, but I helped him.

examples.ko: 가족이어도 말을 안 하면 남남 같아요.
examples.en: Even family feels like strangers if you don't talk.
We share a family name, but we aren't related.

examples.ko: 한 집에 살아도 남남처럼 지내는 부부가 있어요.
examples.en: Some couples live in one house but act like strangers.

examples.ko: 남남끼리 만나서 가족이 되는 게 결혼이에요.
examples.en: Marriage is when two people who were strangers become a family.

explain: '타인'보다 부드러운 입말이고 '남이다'와 비슷하게 써요. 서로 가까운 사이였다가 멀어졌을 때도 '남남이 되다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: If we break up, we become strangers again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가깝던 사이가 완전히 끊어져서 아무 관계도 없게 된다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means a once-close relationship is completely cut off.

explain_en: It is a softer spoken word than '타인' and is used like '남이다'. It is also used when people who were once close drift apart, as in '남남이 되다'.

examples.en: He has exceptionally good manual skill.

examples.ko: 동생은 어릴 때부터 남달리 호기심이 많았어요.
examples.en: My younger brother has been unusually curious since he was little.
This singer has an exceptionally clear voice.
This year it snowed unusually much.

examples.ko: 남달리 노력한 만큼 좋은 결과가 나왔어요.
examples.en: The good result came from working harder than others.
My mother cherished me more than usual.

explain: '유난히'와 비슷하지만 남과 비교해서 특별히 눈에 띈다는 느낌이고, 주로 좋은 점을 말할 때 어울려요. 형용사 '남다르다'와 뜻이 이어져요.
explain_en: It is close to '유난히', but it feels like standing out compared with others, and it mostly suits good qualities. It is connected in meaning to the adjective '남다르다'.

examples.en: He helped needy neighbors without anyone knowing.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 남모르는 고민이 있어 보였어요.
examples.en: That friend seemed to have a worry he kept to himself.

examples.ko: 저는 남모르게 눈물을 흘린 적이 많아요.
examples.en: I have often cried secretly where no one could see.

examples.ko: 남모르는 노력이 있었기에 성공할 수 있었어요.
examples.en: Unseen effort made the success possible.

examples.ko: 집 앞에 꽃이 남모르게 피어 있었어요.
examples.en: Flowers had quietly bloomed in front of the house without anyone noticing.

examples.ko: 남모르게 준비한 선물이니까 비밀로 해 주세요.
examples.en: I prepared this gift secretly, so please keep it quiet.

explain: 거의 '남모르게', '남모르는' 모양으로 써요. '르' 불규칙이라 '남몰라요'가 되고, 같은 뜻으로 '남몰래'라는 부사도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is used almost only as '남모르게' or '남모르는'. It is a 르-irregular verb, so it becomes '남몰라요', and the adverb '남몰래' is also common with the same meaning.

examples.en: Australia is in the southern hemisphere, so December is summer.
In the southern hemisphere the seasons are opposite to the north.
You can see the Southern Cross in the southern sky.
If you travel to the southern hemisphere, it's hot even at Christmas.

examples.ko: 칠레는 남반구에 길게 뻗어 있는 나라예요.
examples.en: Chile is a country stretching long in the southern hemisphere.
The southern and northern hemispheres are divided by the equator.

explain: 짝말은 '북반구'이고, 지구를 적도로 나눌 때 써요. 호주나 뉴질랜드처럼 계절이 한국과 반대인 곳을 이야기할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Its counterpart is '북반구', and it is used when dividing the globe at the equator. It often comes up for places like Australia or New Zealand, where the seasons are opposite to Korea's.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 남성미가 넘치는 역할을 잘해요.
examples.en: That actor plays roles full of masculine charm well.
Thick eyebrows add to his manly appeal.
His manly voice is really attractive.

examples.ko: 그는 거친 남성미보다 부드러운 매력이 있어요.
examples.en: He has a gentle charm rather than rugged masculinity.
A perfume ad emphasizing masculinity came out.
His broad shoulders give off a masculine feel.

explain: 짝말은 '여성미'이고 외모나 분위기, 목소리에서 느끼는 남자다운 멋을 말해요. 사람마다 생각이 달라서 직접 평가할 때는 조심해서 써요.
explain_en: Its counterpart is '여성미', and it describes manly appeal felt in looks, atmosphere or voice. Ideas about it differ among people, so be careful when using it to judge someone directly.

examples.en: He is a person full of masculine appeal.
There are many ads that push a masculine image.
This design has a strong masculine feel.
That novel was written from a male perspective.

examples.ko: 남성적 목소리와 여성적 목소리를 구분해 보세요.
examples.en: Try to tell masculine and feminine voices apart.

examples.ko: 가게 분위기가 남성적 취향에 맞춰져 있어요.
examples.en: The shop's atmosphere is tailored to masculine tastes.

explain: '남성적 매력'처럼 뒤에 명사가 바로 와요. '남성적인 사람', '그 옷은 남성적이에요'처럼 '-인', '-이다'도 붙여 쓰고, 반대말은 '여성적'이에요.
explain_en: A noun follows directly, as in '남성적 매력'. You can also attach '-인' or '-이다', as in '남성적인 사람' or '그 옷은 남성적이에요', and the opposite is '여성적'.

examples.ko: 아이들이 있는 집에서는 남아나는 물건이 없어요.
examples.en: In a house with kids, nothing survives intact.

examples.ko: 이렇게 험하게 쓰면 신발이 남아나지 않아요.
examples.en: If you wear shoes this roughly, they won't last.
My salary doesn't stay with me, and I'm worried.

examples.ko: 친구들이 다 먹어서 남아나는 과자가 없어요.
examples.en: My friends ate everything, so no snacks are left.

examples.ko: 이사하는 동안 남아난 그릇이 하나도 없었어요.
examples.en: Not a single dish survived the move.
Because of the cat, no curtain survives.

explain: 거의 부정문에서 '~이/가 남아나지 않는다', '남아나는 게 없다'로 써요. 물건이 계속 망가지거나 돈이 금방 없어질 때 투덜대는 느낌으로 말해요.
explain_en: It is used almost only in negative forms like '~이/가 남아나지 않는다' or '남아나는 게 없다'. It carries a grumbling tone when things keep breaking or money vanishes quickly.

en: be enough; be sufficient; be superfluous

examples.en: Rice is in surplus these days, so the price dropped.

examples.ko: 시간이 너무 남아돌아서 책을 한 권 읽었어요.
examples.en: I had so much spare time that I read a book.
There were more staff than needed, so I left work early.
When there is extra food, I share it with the neighbors.
He has so much energy to spare that he runs around even at night.
I'm not rich enough to have money to spare.

explain: '남다'보다 필요한 양보다 훨씬 많아서 넘친다는 느낌이 강해요. 'ㄹ' 탈락이 있어서 '남아도는'으로 변하니 주의하세요.
explain_en: Compared with '남다', it strongly suggests there is far more than needed. Note the ㄹ-drop in forms like '남아도는'.

examples.ko: 어머니는 성실한 사람이 좋은 남편감이라고 하세요.
examples.en: My mother says a diligent person makes good husband material.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 어디 내놔도 훌륭한 남편감이에요.
examples.en: He's excellent husband material anywhere.
They say it's not easy to find good husband material.
My aunt introduced me to a decent prospective husband.

examples.ko: 요리 잘하는 남자가 인기 있는 남편감이래요.
examples.en: They say men who cook well are popular husband material.
My friend wants a kind person as a husband.

explain: '-감'은 어떤 역할에 어울리는 후보를 말해서 '신랑감', '사윗감'처럼 써요. 사람을 조건으로 평가하는 느낌이 있어서 말할 상황을 가려 쓰세요.
explain_en: The suffix '-감' means a candidate suited for a role, as in '신랑감' and '사윗감'. It can sound like judging a person by conditions, so choose the situation carefully.

examples.ko: 우리 아기는 낯가림이 심해서 처음 보는 사람 품에 안 가요.
examples.en: My baby is shy with strangers and won't go into a new person's arms.

examples.ko: 저는 낯가림이 있어서 새 모임이 어색해요.
examples.en: I'm shy around new people, so new gatherings feel awkward.

examples.ko: 낯가림 때문에 처음에는 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: Because I'm shy with strangers, I couldn't even speak at first.

examples.ko: 동생은 낯가림이 없어서 누구하고나 잘 놀아요.
examples.en: My younger sibling isn't shy and plays well with anyone.
As my shyness with strangers lessened, I made more friends.
They say a child's stranger shyness is part of growing up.

explain: 동사 '낯을 가리다'의 명사형으로 '낯가림이 심하다/없다'처럼 써요. 아기의 낯가림과 어른의 성격을 말할 때 둘 다 써요.
explain_en: It is the noun form of the verb '낯을 가리다' and is used as '낯가림이 심하다/없다'. It describes both a baby's stranger anxiety and an adult's personality.

examples.en: Do you sell this snack individually too?
I want to buy single pieces, not a box.
It's individually wrapped, so it's easy to carry.
These batteries are not sold individually.
The single-piece price is a bit higher than the bundle.

examples.ko: 사탕이 낱개로 들어 있어서 나눠 먹기 좋아요.
examples.en: The candies come in single pieces, so they're easy to share.

explain: '묶음', '한 상자'의 반대 개념으로 보통 '낱개로'라는 모양으로 써요. 가게에서 물건을 하나씩 살 수 있는지 물어볼 때 유용해요.
explain_en: It is the opposite of '묶음' or '한 상자' and usually appears as '낱개로'. It is useful when asking in a shop whether you can buy items one at a time.

examples.en: I separated the documents into single sheets and scanned them.
The book is old, so loose pages have come off.
Loose sheets of paper are easy to lose.

examples.ko: 이 달력은 낱장을 한 장씩 뜯어 써요.
examples.en: You tear off this calendar's sheets one by one.
I asked whether single-sheet printing was possible.
Write a number on every single sheet.

explain: 묶이거나 제본되지 않은 한 장 한 장의 종이를 말하고 반대는 '묶음'이나 '제본'이에요. 낱개, 낱말처럼 '낱-'은 하나하나라는 느낌을 더해요.
explain_en: It refers to individual sheets that are not bound together, and the opposites are '묶음' or '제본'. Like 낱개 and 낱말, the prefix '낱-' adds a sense of one-by-one.
